setting: A fictional phone call to the reception desk of a small city clinic.

presentation.situation: You phone City Clinic to make an appointment. The receptionist, {{name}}, can offer {{slot_a}} or {{slot_b}}. {{full}} is fully booked. Say why you are calling, choose a time, and confirm the details.
presentation.opening: Good morning, City Clinic, this is {{name}}. How can I help you?

brief.you_are: You are a patient calling a clinic.
brief.situation: You need to see a doctor. The clinic can offer {{slot_a}} or {{slot_b}}.
brief.task: Say why you are calling, choose one of the times, then repeat the day and time to confirm.
brief.done_looks_like: You and the receptionist both know the day and the time of your appointment.

participants.name: You
participants.relationship: Calling the clinic for an appointment

participants.name: {{name}}
participants.relationship: Answers the phone at City Clinic

card.want: Book the patient into a free slot and get their name for the diary.
card.attitude: Polite, calm and a little busy.
card.speech: Very simple, clear English. Short sentences. One question at a time.
tactics: Offer only the times you have
Ask them to say the time back if they have not confirmed it

pressure.challenging: Polite and brisk, like a busy desk.

ledger.text: City Clinic has free appointments on {{slot_a}} and {{slot_b}}.
An appointment with the doctor lasts about {{length}} minutes.
New patients should bring a photo ID.

objectives.evidence: The learner says they want an appointment or why they need to see the doctor.
alternatives: I need to see a doctor
I'd like to make an appointment

objectives.evidence: The learner chooses or asks for a specific time.
alternatives: Tuesday at ten is good for me

objectives.evidence: The learner repeats the day and time, or asks the receptionist to confirm them.

examples: I'm calling to make an appointment.
So that's Tuesday at ten. Thank you.
prerequisites: Look at the free times in the briefing.

beats.goal: Find out why they are calling.
opportunity: Would you like to make an appointment?
Do you want to see the doctor?
beats.orient: You are calling the clinic. I am the receptionist. Please say: I want to make an appointment.
fallback: How can I help you today?
Do you want to see the doctor?

beats.goal: Agree a day and time from the free slots.
opportunity: I have {{slot_a}} or {{slot_b}}. Which is better for you?
beats.orient: Now choose a time. I have {{slot_a}} or {{slot_b}}. Please choose one.
fallback: I have {{slot_a}} or {{slot_b}}. Which is better for you?
Which day is good for you?

beats.goal: Get the patient to say the booked time back.
opportunity: Can you say the day and time back to me, please?
Is that all correct for you?
beats.orient: We are almost finished. Please say your day and time again, so we both know.
fallback: Please tell me the day and time again.
Please bring a photo ID. Is that all right?

closing_line: Thank you. See you then. Goodbye!

o1.good: Saying right away why you are calling, so the other person can help quickly.
common_mistakes: Waiting for the receptionist to guess
o1.micro_lesson: On the phone, say your reason first. 'I'm calling to' is a useful start.
o1.model: I'm calling to make an appointment.

o2.good: Choosing clearly from the times offered.
common_mistakes: Answering 'yes' to a choice of two times
o2.micro_lesson: When you get two choices, say the one you want, not 'yes'.
o2.model: Tuesday at ten is good for me.
o2.smaller_step: Say only the day you want.

o3.good: Repeating the day and time so nobody is confused.
o3.micro_lesson: Repeat important details. It stops mistakes and it is polite on the phone.
o3.model: So that's Tuesday at ten. Thank you.
o3.smaller_step: Say your day and your time once more.
